### Blind extraction

1. announce-use: Announce at the start that this skill is in use, by name. (SKILL.md:12)
2. green-suite-first: Run the project's full test suite on the tree about to be integrated; when it fails, show the failures and stop, offering no integration until it passes. (SKILL.md:14-26, 193)
3. workspace-detection: Tell a normal repository, a named-branch worktree and a detached-HEAD worktree apart by comparing the git directory with the common git directory, and capture the worktree path before changing directory, because cleanup needs it later. (SKILL.md:28-44)
4. base-branch-confirm: Take the base branch from the plan, the conversation or the branch's upstream, and when it is not known ask the person to confirm a guess before merging. (SKILL.md:46-51, 200)
5. integration-menu: Present exactly three options (merge locally, push and open a pull request, keep as is), or two on a detached HEAD with no merge, and wait for the person's choice; integration is the person's decision. (SKILL.md:53-82, 194)
6. local-merge: Merge locally by moving to the main checkout, checking out and pulling the base, merging the branch and running the tests on the merged result; on a failing result stop, leaving the branch and worktree in place. (SKILL.md:86-104, 199)
7. merged-cleanup: After a green merged result, remove the worktree and then delete the branch with a safe delete. (SKILL.md:106-111)
8. push-and-pr: Push the branch with upstream tracking (from a detached HEAD, to a new remote branch) and open a pull request against the base with the forge's tooling, following the repository's template, and report its address. (SKILL.md:113-124)
9. keep-worktree: Keep the worktree after a pull request is opened or the branch is kept, because review fixes are made there, until the work lands. (SKILL.md:126, 128-130, 197)
10. discard-on-request: Discard only when the person explicitly asks, never as an offered option: list the branch, its commits and the worktree, require the typed word discard, then remove the worktree and force-delete the branch. (SKILL.md:78-82, 132-157, 195-196)
11. provenance-cleanup: Remove a worktree only when this skill created it (it lives under .worktrees/ or worktrees/), from outside it, then prune; leave any other worktree and a detached one to the host. (SKILL.md:159-178, 198)
12. no-force-on-reject: A rejected push means the remote moved: investigate, and force-push only on the person's explicit request. (SKILL.md:201)

Adopted, pending cr-p3em.4, into the Autopilot-full playbook and delivered there in this round: trunk is merged into the feature's branch (git merge --no-ff --no-commit), the staged merge is gated (never refused as empty), its manual checks done before the commit, then committed as one commit of the whole index (git commit --no-edit, not land), checked to have both parents and the results noted with the merge commit's SHA; then the commit gate runs with --since on the committed tip with a clean tree, prints the exact range it judged, and each manual check it prints is done on that range and noted on the bead with the range and the tip's SHA. The checks given the judged range read the same range the gate prints. Nothing is pushed for the pull request until both pass; a failure is fixed by a new gated commit and the step runs again, and a tip with nothing changed since trunk stops the feature as nothing to ship. The gate judges that tip: it reads its gate file from HEAD and refuses a working copy that differs or is not a regular file, its whitespace check reads the merge-base..HEAD range, not the empty index, and the trunk merge's own commit is gated even when it brings no change (.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full/commit_gate.py, tests/checks/test_commit_gate.py). It runs the project's own checks for what the branch changed, from the project's gate file, rather than one fixed test command. A playbook cannot be a report's compared unit, so the row is absent and the adopt is pended, then completed once the playbook lists it.
